name: Narration: how a web request travels

setup.topic: Narrate how a web request travels from the browser to the server and back.

script.topic: Narrate how a web request travels from the browser to the server and back.

questions.title: URL to response
questions.prompt: Walk me through what happens after you type a URL and press Enter. Narrate it like you're explaining to a teammate.
keyPoints: URL parsing and browser cache check
probes: Which transport does the DNS lookup usually use?
What changes when the URL is HTTPS?
redFlags: Says the browser connects to the domain name directly

questions.title: DNS transport
questions.prompt: Which transport does a typical DNS lookup use?

choices.text: UDP on port 53, falling back to TCP for large replies

questions.title: Caching layers
questions.prompt: Where along that path can a response be cached?
probes: How does the browser decide a cached copy is still fresh?

chunks.text: Okay so first the browser parses the URL
and checks whether it already has a cached copy.
If not it needs the IP address, so it does a DNS lookup.
That goes to the resolver, then the root, the TLD, and the authoritative server.
Then it opens a connection to the server
and sends the HTTP GET request, and the server sends back HTML which the browser renders.
My answer: UDP on port 53, falling back to TCP for large replies
The browser caches responses based on Cache-Control headers, and a CDN can cache in between.
